title: How the world’s fires changed while humanity hit pause
summary: COVID-19 lockdowns cut global fire activity by 12.3 percent.
llm_summary: During the COVID‑19 lockdowns, the sudden drop in travel, industry and other human activities slashed global fire activity by roughly 12 percent. Satellite data show that fewer emissions, reduced deforestation pressure and a slowdown in agricultural burning all contributed to the dip, highlighting how quickly our collective behavior can reshape the planet’s fire regime
